name: FastFrames (S 1.3B and L 14B)

lineage.how_derived: S keeps the frozen two-step frame-wise Causal Forcing++ generator and trains a pixel decoder and a KV refinement network around it; L distills Wan2.1-14B into a two-step causal model (Causal Forcing++ recipe) and then trains pixel decoder and KV refiner the same way (card)

purpose: Autoregressive two-step video diffusion models that generate 480p video at interactive latency (paper: VAE decoding and KV-cache updates were over half of end-to-end latency and are replaced by lightweight networks); targets real-time camera- and physics-conditioned generation.

license.name: Apple Machine Learning Research Model License (apple-amlr)
license.notes: LICENSE of apple/FastFrames-S read: use, copy, modify, distribute and create derivatives exclusively for Research Purposes (non-commercial scientific research; excludes commercial exploitation, product development and use in any commercial product or service); redistribution needs a copy of the agreement and an attribution notice, derivatives must be identified; revocable, terminable on breach. Same license named on the FastFrames-L card (its LICENSE file not separately read). The LingBot parts are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the code uses the Apple Sample Code License (card). Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.kind: autoregressive causal video diffusion transformer, two denoising steps per frame, plus separate KV-refinement network and lightweight pixel decoder instead of the VAE decoder

variants.format: safetensors (pixel decoder 0.26 GB, KV refiner 0.69 GB; plus a LingBot variant 0.82 GB)
variants.notes: 1.3B per card; the repo holds only the added networks, the frozen Causal Forcing++ generator is taken from the base repo (size not read here); outputs 832x480, 81 frames at 16 fps

variants.format: safetensors (DiT 28.58 GB, KV refiner 1.78 GB, pixel decoder 0.29 GB)
variants.notes: 14B per card; plus 142.89 GB of intermediate checkpoints (causal teacher, consistency, DMD) in the same repo

pc-12gb.notes: S weights are small, but the latency figures are B200 and the card requires Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA GPU; no AMD data. L: no (30.64 GB BF16).

pc-32gb.notes: 30.64 GB of weights; the vendor runs L on 8 GPUs for its 45 ms per frame figure

benchmarks.name: Latency per frame, 480p
benchmarks.variant: FastFrames-S, single B200 (paper abstract); card profile on 1 GPU: 35.4 ms

strengths: Interactive latency: 28 and 22 responses per second claimed (paper abstract)
S claimed to match a state-of-the-art model nearly 8x slower in quality (paper abstract, VBench table not read)
weaknesses: Only NVIDIA CUDA reference code; L needs a multi-GPU node for the quoted latency
soft.maturity: Apple Machine Learning Research; paper arXiv 2611.23226 (2026).

tona_fit.reason: Two-step causal video diffusion with lightweight decoder and KV refiner; S is small enough for any class, but video generation is outside Tona's coding-agent purpose, so it is prior art for a possible own video path.
